## feature

### Per-read reason tag, chimeric_read subtype, and merge-stats table

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: implemented end to end, suite green with new tests, and the pilot
equivalence gate passes with exactly the two intended deltas.

#### description

```
type: [text, table]
```

1. `ZM:Z:<reason>` on both primary records of every unmerged failed
   template (`--reason-tag`, default `ZM`, validated distinct from `ZC`
   and the `ZR` marker). Merged and unaligned-only templates carry no
   reason tag.
2. `chimeric_read`: cross-contig pairs whose mates show read-through
   evidence — an outer soft clip of at least 10 bp occurring in the other
   mate's stored sequence — reported instead of `different_contig`
   (memoized; off the hot path).
3. `--merge-stats-parquet` (optional, explicit path): long-format table
   `type` (classification | reason | family | overlap_hist), `key`,
   `count`, deterministic ordering; family rollup groups all reasons plus
   unaligned and merged.

| Pilot observation | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| `different_contig` before / after split | 453 → 242 + 211 `chimeric_read` |
| Overlap histogram sum | 97,748 = mergeable count |
| Reason rows | match the done-line merge-reasons dict exactly |

#### before

The failure reason was computed per template, counted into the stderr
done line, and discarded — no output said which reason applied to which
read; `different_contig` conflated concatemer evidence with plain
cross-contig misassignment.

#### after

Every unmerged failed template's primaries name their reason in-place;
concatemers are distinguishable from plain cross-contig pairs; QC can
consume the family rollup and overlap histogram from one parquet file.
Record content is otherwise byte-identical (gate-verified).

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `EQUIVALENCE: PASS` on the pilot with `--strip-tag ZM
  --normalize-reason-split` (records identical modulo the new tag; done
  line identical after summing the contig split).
- `238 passed, 9 skipped`; ruff lint/format clean; pilot wall ~6.5 s
  (unchanged).

:::

## fix

None

## limitation

### The chimeric evidence test is clip-containment, not alignment

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: the check is deliberately cheap and sequence-local; it can miss
read-through whose clip is shorter than 10 bp or heavily errored, and it
cannot distinguish a concatemer from a true cross-molecule chimera.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

The subtype answers "is there read-through evidence consistent with a
concatemer or chimera", not "is this molecule a dimer". Consumers wanting
structural certainty can align the merged read (as the benchmark did:
split primary+supplementary alignments).

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

The benchmark's `fastp_only.se.bam` export shows both signatures:
`chimeric_read`-class pairs split primary+supplementary; plain
`different_contig` pairs do not.

:::

## conclusion

### The augment design shipped with no behavior change beyond the two intended deltas

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: the equivalence gate pins it — records identical modulo `ZM`, done
line identical after the documented contig split, both parquets and all
other counts untouched.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Outputs: only `ZM` tags and the reason split are new.
2. Performance: pilot wall unchanged; the tag write and clip test run on
   unmerged templates only.
3. Semantics: the reason vocabulary is the 19 documented strings plus
   `chimeric_read`; families are a pure rollup.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`benchmarks/equivalence_check.py --strip-tag ZM --normalize-reason-split`
→ PASS; suite 238.

:::

## observation

### The pilot's different_contig split is nearly even

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: measured directly on the pilot.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

453 cross-contig refusals split into 242 plain `different_contig` and
211 `chimeric_read` — consistent with the benchmark's finding that the
fastp-only cross-contig population is concatemer-heavy.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Pilot done line after the change; the walkthrough pair
(F1-942|F1-1194, flags 65/129 with 80M70S mates) is exactly the
clip-containment signature.

:::

## process

### Plan first, gate with explicit tolerances, keep the vocabulary closed

```
status: right
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The plan's verification criteria were written before code; the gate
   options encode the two allowed deltas rather than eyeballing.
2. The reason vocabulary was left closed (19 strings + chimeric_read);
   families are presentation, not new semantics.
3. The chimeric check was designed off the hot path (memoized, run only
   on cross-contig refusals) — pilot wall confirmed unchanged.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Plan `20261026-114810` (as executed); gate output in the session log.

:::

### Two test-harness stumbles cost a few minutes each

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Tests initially built records against a nonexistent `fx.header`
   attribute and stale contig names ("ctg1"/"ctg2") from an earlier
   mental draft; both failed loudly and were fixed against the fixture's
   real API.
2. The better action: read the fixture API before writing tests, not
   after the failures.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

AttributeError/`mapped records without reference id` failures in the
session log.

:::
